claim_boundary: This catalog records discovered sources and interface facts. V4 automatic selection is determined separately by access status, research-use status, evidence tier, use mode, frozen spatial/geology compatibility, and execution context; legacy production_eligible is compatibility-only. Catalog inclusion is not scientific endorsement.

coverage.notes: 867 physical sediment/loess/paleosol samples, 799 distinct reported coordinate pairs and 6,069 As/Cr/Cu/Hg/Ni/Pb/Zn observations; 222 samples are in Junggar, 170 in Tarim, 39 on the eastern Tibetan Plateau and 63 in Qaidam.

license.notes: The official Figshare API declares CC0. Dataset DOI, author and repository identity are retained as scientific attribution.

limitations: The continental-scale source materially improves northern and western China coverage but is not a complete national probability grid.
The publisher does not declare a datum, CRS or positional uncertainty, so numeric coordinates remain reported-only and are not silently promoted to WGS84.
The pinned README maps As, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn to analytical methods and digestion/preparation; it does not map Hg to a method.
Dataset-level field duplicates, blind laboratory replicates and reference materials are documented, but row-level QC assignments and acceptance results are not published.
Survey-area labels are geographic context rather than matched geologic units.
4tu-northern-china-sediment.title: Raw data of Geochemical Compositions of Surface Sediments in Northern China

coverage.notes: The release contains 2,002 topsoil and subsoil samples from 51 LDSF sentinel sites. It is broad multi-country evidence, not a continuous or statistically uniform African grid.

license.notes: Version 2.0 terms specify CC BY 4.0; retain dataset and article citations.

limitations: The LDSF field design and available archived samples are not uniform national or continental coverage.
Aqua-regia results are quasi-total and must remain separate from total or differently extracted soil values.
One hundred twenty-six samples have no coordinates and cannot enter coordinate-dependent mapping without additional evidence.
The source contains negative numeric instrument results and many positive values below source-wide DL or QL; these remain explicit quality flags.
Raw country labels SAfrica and Zimbambwe require a separate normalization field while retaining the publisher strings.
The registered files and related article do not state the coordinate reference system, so the adapter does not assert EPSG:4326.
The variable workbook describes As.75 as Arsenic-78 and reports 2009-2013 sampling, while the related paper reports 2009-2012; these metadata conflicts require source-level review.
afsis-phase-i-wet-chemistry.title: AfSIS Phase I archived soil samples: wet chemistry data

coverage.notes: Ongoing Alaska database combining DGGS, USGS, BLM and former U.S. Bureau of Mines records, including modern laboratory spreadsheets and legacy reports.

license.notes: Recent DGGS raw-data releases state an open end-user licence, while the integrated database also contains federal and legacy sources. Acceptance must occur per publication or upstream contributor.

limitations: The database mixes scanned legacy reports, federal databases and direct laboratory imports; original publication and analytical lineage must remain record-level facts.
The dynamic all-record export is not itself an immutable version; prefer pinned DGGS publication packages for the first adapter.
Coordinate datums and method packages vary between releases.
alaska-dggs-webgeochem.publisher: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys
alaska-dggs-webgeochem.title: Alaska Geochemistry Database (WebGeochem)

coverage.notes: SIGAM exposes multielement chemistry and locations for stream-sediment and soil samples; SEGEMAR annual reports describe more than 40,000 stream-sediment records.

license.notes: The service identifies itself as an open geospatial data catalogue, but the exact research-use, download and attribution notice must be captured from each selected metadata record.

limitations: The stated total spans historical archive samples and newer SEGEMAR sampling; date, method and coordinate uncertainty differ by project.
The 54-element map description is a regional cartographic product and does not prove identical analyte coverage for every record.
Repository PDFs, SIGAM layers and sheet products can repeat the same survey samples.
argentina-segemar-geochemistry.title: SIGAM multielement geochemical sample data

coverage.notes: 1,315 catchment-outlet sites across Australia; 2,623 nonblank <75 µm determinations per requested element. This is an ultra-low-density national survey, not a regular grid or local prediction surface.

license.notes: The 2011 CSV itself states CC BY 3.0 Australia. The current portal displays CC BY 4.0 International; the registry conservatively retains the contemporaneous file-level licence and records the version difference.

limitations: Catchment-outlet transported regolith is not interchangeable with in-situ topsoil or stream sediment.
The sampling density is designed for national-scale patterns, not site-scale prediction.
TOS/BOS depths, grain fractions and total/aqua-regia/MMI analytical bases remain separate.
The adapter extracts only <75 µm ICP-MS As, Cu, Pb and Zn and excludes field duplicates from independent-sample selection.
Coordinate positional accuracy is not reported by the publisher and remains explicitly unavailable.
australia-ngsa.title: National Geochemical Survey of Australia: Geochemical Atlas dataset

coverage.notes: 2,396 TOS/BOS records at 1,247 sites across seven states and territories; national catchment survey rather than a regular grid.

license.notes: The publisher file states CC BY 4.0 Australia; retain dataset DOI and Geoscience Australia attribution.

limitations: Only Hg is present in this product; it does not supply the other target elements.
Top and bottom outlet sediment are separate horizons and cannot be pooled without an explicit comparison decision.
The reported 0.01 ng Hg limit is a mass LOD, not a concentration-row threshold.
Duplicate codes identify QA/QC structure and do not create independent spatial sites.
Catchment sampling is nationally broad but spatially discrete and uneven.
australia-ngsa-mercury.title: National Geochemical Survey of Australia: Mercury Concentrations Dataset

coverage.notes: National compilation of located whole-rock and stream-sediment analyses from Geoscience Australia and other surveys.

license.notes: Current product-specific licensing and any contributed state data exceptions need confirmation.

limitations: Discovery located official legacy documentation but not a verified current bulk numeric endpoint.
Contributed state-survey records may overlap upstream releases.
australia-ozchem.title: OZCHEM National Whole Rock and Stream Sediment Geochemistry Database

coverage.notes: Long-running baseline survey of soil, stream sediment, stream water and panned concentrates across the UK.

license.notes: Derived grids are OGL; underpinning survey point observations require a separate BGS licence and are not open-only production data.

limitations: Open interpolated grids are derived products and cannot substitute for source point observations.
Point data cannot enter the open-only production route without a compatible explicit licence.
bgs-gbase.title: Geochemical Baseline Survey of the Environment (G-BASE)

license.notes: Open access is stated for repository items, but reuse/redistribution terms for the integrated service need verification.

brazil-sgb-geochemistry.title: GeoSGB integrated geochemical samples

license.notes: The release is publicly downloadable through the provincial site; the exact Open Government Licence notice and any third-party conditions from the 116 original sources must be bound to the selected files before use.

limitations: The compilation integrates 116 original releases, so independence and duplicate handling must follow the original survey and sample identifiers.
Eighteen analytical methods and laboratories cannot be combined without record-level method mapping.
Vegetation and moss-mat observations fall outside the current four-media production contract and require separate medium terms.

limitations: The source contains 15 samples from one volcanic-plutonic complex and cannot close a province-wide or national rock-coverage gap.
The workbook does not declare a coordinate CRS or positional accuracy, so coordinates remain reported-only rather than silently becoming WGS84.

coverage.notes: The audited As/Cr/Cu/Hg/Ni/Pb/Zn subset contains 3,739,180 target observations representing 689,291 station-date-time-depth sampling events at 17,248 stations in 35 countries. River, lake, groundwater, reservoir and wetland coverage is spatially and temporally uneven.

license.notes: The v3 Zenodo record and included README identify CC BY 4.0; retain archive citation and record DOI.

limitations: The seven-element subset covers 35 voluntarily contributing countries and is not a uniform global freshwater grid.
Dissolved, extractable, suspended and total operational fractions must remain separate; Cr-VI is excluded from elemental chromium.
Only 279,225 of 3,739,180 target observations have a defined analysis method, so method-comparable subsets are substantially smaller.
The source contains 1,836,306 censored values plus Pending review and Suspect rows that remain traceable and must be filtered according to use.
Rows for different elements or fractions at the same station, date, time and depth are one physical sampling event, not independent evidence.
The v3 description claims 22,982 stations and 622 parameters, while the selected metadata files contain 22,981 rows and 621 parameters.
Eleven required ZIP members were locally range-verified by DOI/version, byte ranges, member names, decoded sizes, schema and row counts; the complete 201 MB archive was not downloaded locally.

georoc-database.title: GEOROC Database

coverage.notes: The full IDP2025 product reports 123 cruises and 4,097 stations across all packages. The verified discrete-seawater collection exposes 4,094 stations and 82 cruise labels; the Cu/Ni/Zn OR-filtered export contains target-bearing samples from 46 cruises and 1,550 cruise-station pairs.

license.notes: Fair Use Agreement requires IDP and original data-contributor citations.

limitations: Cruise-track ocean sampling is not uniform global surface-water coverage.
Dissolved, particulate and other fractions plus quality flags and contributor citations must remain distinct.
The official IDP2025 seawater parameter inventory contains dissolved Cu, Ni and Zn but no arsenic variable; another water source is required for As.
The frozen webODV export preserves nmol/kg. It must not be mixed with ug/L without an explicit element-specific atomic-mass and seawater-density conversion.
SeaDataNet flags 3 and 4 identify probably-bad and bad values; they remain traceable raw records but are excluded from the demonstration slice.
The adapter and 30-row review sheet are prepared, but named human review is still incomplete.

Sample ID 78013 occurs twice in each file and must be joined by occurrence order.

limitations: The database contains natural elements and anthropogenic contaminants; target-analyte scope must be selected explicitly.

The verified public API export is dynamic and timestamped; the selected inorganic response is fixed by request, scientific data/member hashes, byte counts and row statistics but has no matching immutable DOI. The outer ZIP and information filename may drift only when the pinned scientific data and method members remain byte-identical and the information text still proves the frozen query semantics.
The As, Cu, Ni and Zn measurements are reported on a dry-weight basis after partial nitric-acid digestion and must not be represented as total content.
Batch metadata mix accredited and not-accredited analyses, and the export can repeat a sample across parameter groups; both facts must survive record-level mapping.

Repeated seasons, campaigns, depths and land-use classes are non-independent and remain explicit.

limitations: Repository search results are not one harmonised geochemical dataset.

sweden-sgu-geochemical-atlas.title: Geochemical Atlas of Sweden data

coverage.notes: The release contains 1,314 O-, A- and C-horizon samples from 166 sites in 30 mountain ecosystems and five climate zones. It is a targeted mountain survey, not a spatially continuous or nationally representative China soil grid.

license.notes: The dataset metadata records licence code 1, which the TPDC interface maps to CC BY 4.0. Retain the dataset DOI, authors and TPDC attribution.

limitations: The survey covers 30 mountain ecosystems and cannot be described as uniform nationwide China coverage.
The release contains Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn among the project targets but does not contain As or Hg.
O, A and C horizons are scientifically distinct and must remain separate sample types and comparison groups.
The source records GPS coordinates but the registered metadata and data files do not declare a coordinate reference system; no EPSG code may be inferred.
Three site labels (SN5, SN6 and SN7) have more than one published coordinate pair and must retain sample-level coordinates rather than a forced site centroid.

The separate bulk-density workbook can fill 58 missing main-table rows, but six non-missing bulk-density values and five coordinates conflict with the main workbook; supplemental values must never overwrite published main-table values silently.

The main workbook has no row-level detection-limit, qualifier or method fields. Dataset-level preparation, digestion, ICP-AES/ICP-MS and QC evidence comes from the linked article and must carry dataset or publication scope.

wosis.title: World Soil Information Service (WoSIS)

coverage.notes: 1,022,092 whole-rock analyses (1,006,397 with reported coordinates); measured 2026-08-21: country=cn 26,551 rows with 74,384 As/Cr/Cu/Ni/Pb/Zn values, southern-Tibet window (88-99E, 27-31.5N) 1,301 rows, Russia 24,671 rows. About 68 percent of citations resolve to GEOROC, so coverage overlaps the georoc-* lineage and is not an independent replication.

license.notes: Zenodo record metadata declares license id cc-by-4.0. Retain the dataset DOI and cite Gard, Hasterok & Halpin (2019, ESSD).

limitations: Sampling dates are not published; the age columns are geological rock ages in Ma and must never be read as collection times.
Coordinates are retained as reported without a declared datum and are not asserted to be WGS 84.
About 68 percent of resolved citations come from GEOROC; records overlapping georoc-* compilations are the same literature lineage, not independent replication.
Analytical method metadata is sparse (frequently 'not given'); method fields stay empty rather than being guessed.
The compilation snapshot ends in 2019 and adds no post-2019 literature.

Ninety-three samples from two river systems add lineage diversity, not regional statistical representativeness.
